newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin says on track to balance budget.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin says on track to balance budget.

text.p: Canada's Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Wednesday the federal government was clearly on track to a balanced budget.

"We are very clearly on a track to a balanced budget. We've always said that was our ultimate objective," Martin told reporters after telling the House of Commons finance committee that he projected a 1998/99 deficit of C$9 billion or one percent of gross domestic product.
He declined to say when the budget would be balanced.

He refused to be drawn on making a substantial cut in unemployment insurance premiums. The portion that employees must pay are forecast in Martin's budget to fall to C$2.90 per C$100 of insurable earnings in 1997 from C$2.95 in 1996 -- far less of a cut than opposition politicians are demanding.
"I would like to bring them (the rates) down. Nobody would like to bring them down as much as I would," Martin said.

"That being said, I think we've got to recognize that the worst thing that happened in the last recession is when the previous government was forced in the middle of the recession to cut benefits and hike rates, because if there was anything that prolonged it, it was certainly that counterproductive cost."
He added that the premiums were part of the government's revenues. That would mean that any reduction would affect the government's deficit figures unless corresponding spending cuts were made.
